parsed_action.body:
Information interactions and failure migration require distinguishing behaviorally active mechanisms from those that earned a role. The I1–I4 run demonstrated that batch ingress and semantic sidecars were behaviorally active, producing genuine cross-source prose, yet no cumulative task-artifact work emerged [S02][S08]. The sidecar functioned as semantic state rather than an exact partial charter or independently checkable task artifact [S08].

Failure migration occurred in several ways. Scheduled low-occupancy reentry failed to earn a default role, disrupting qualified code trajectories while reducing cache reuse [S10]. The I1 relief event replaced a one-line body with a receipt costing 79 more tokens, censors the full E40 matrix, and remains descriptive rather than validating broader utility [S02][S10].

The detached-sidecar versus task-artifact gap is confirmed. The work sidecar produced genuine cross-source prose but shed earlier citations, citing only four sources despite 13/14 allowlists [S02]. It was not a versioned partial charter, requirement/evidence matrix with task semantics, or section artifact whose effects could be taken up and checked [S08].

The next system question is semantic persistence × exact incremental task-artifact externalization × candidate-bound verification and repair under common host-owned capacity safety and live evidence ingress [S08]. This moves the program beyond asking whether semantic state can be emitted, focusing on coupling interpretation to durable, exact, independently checkable task work.
parsed_action.heading: Information interactions and failure migration
